goal: Research Israeli commercial TV rate card and how it maps to the existing pricing engine
work_done: Searched for Reshet 13 and Keshet 12 rate cards (no public rate card found; all are negotiated)
Found CPP ranges from a Globes article about Reshet 13 price increases (source: globes.co.il/news/article.aspx?did=1001268924)
Found flat spot price ranges from multiple Israeli media agency pages
Read IARB measurement methodology: 700-household Kantar Focal Meter panel, ~2,200 individuals, Instar tool
Read Second Authority regulations: 10 min ads/hour, 90s max spot, 10s max sponsorship, placement rules
Confirmed: Israel sells on CPP (cost per rating point), 30s spot is the base unit, 15s at ~60-75% of 30s rate
Confirmed standard dayparts: morning, off-prime, semi-prime, news, prime (20:00-23:00), super-prime, late night
Confirmed sponsorship format is 6-10 seconds (regulatory max 10s), appears before/after program and around breaks
Confirmed position premiums exist in the market (first/last commands premium)
Could not find: a published rate card with actual CPP numbers from official Reshet or Keshet source
notes: CPP numbers from Globes article are the most credible found; they match the order of magnitude of the existing engine's ILS 60/sec/TVR base. The existing engine base matches the Israeli market structure well. Key gap: CPP is measured per 30-second spot in Israeli practice, but the engine uses per-second. These are equivalent by multiplication.
